Added tests/test_capacity_snapshot_parity.py: 7 tests build one shared weighted-capacity source snapshot (three 0.25-weight running claims, an explicit weight-2.0 parked waiter blocked by weight/runner-count conditions, a parked waiter with unrecognized/invalid weight, and a live claim with unrecognized weight) and prove that runtime admission (runner_capacity_snapshot), sase agent list -j (agent_list_entries/_agent_to_json), and the ACE TUI (refresh_runner_slot_context, AgentInfoPanel capacity header text, queue detail text, badges) all agree on occupied capacity, effective limit, queue order/position, blockers, and eligibility when built from that one snapshot. Also proves: a remote agent's non-default weight badge never charges the local capacity snapshot; per-project CLI filtering and TUI fold-collapsing never recompute the shared global queue numbers (position/size stay identical pre- and post-filter); and a single live claim with unrecognized weight fails the whole snapshot closed (blocks even a previously-eligible waiter) identically across all three surfaces. Verified: pytest on the new file (7 passed); just fmt/ruff/mypy/keep-sorted all pass on it; ran the full just test-scoped lane (40391 passed, 21 failed) and confirmed by rerunning without the new file that all 21 failures, plus the red lint (feature flags)/lint (symvision)/lint (test waits) gates, pre-date and are independent of this change -- recorded as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP notes on this bead for the epic land agent to triage. sase bead epic-symbols sase-z4.6.5.4.3 reports no --epic-symbol entries for this phase.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: creation-time gate auto-resolution (GateSpec.auto.enabled=True, handled by notification_gates/service.py _resolve_auto_gate) never binds bind_gate_shell_execution_callbacks, so its execute_gate_selection call never claims runner-slot weighted capacity via wait_for_runner_slot -- unlike the answer-time routes (synchronous default and detached, both via notification_gates/cli_answer.py._answer, which this phase covers and proves real). If a shell-backed gate is ever created with auto.enabled=True and an option whose command spawns a real subprocess, that command would run with zero runner-slot accounting. I read "approved automatic" in this phase's description as the answer-time synchronous route (the natural reading paired with "detached", and the only one with the precedent of a fixed defect -- the original sase-z4.6 landing_repairs plan named notification_gates/cli_answer.py calling the executor without capacity acquisition as a confirmed bug, now fixed), not GateSpec.auto.enabled, which is a separate, older, creation-time mechanism with no confirmed-broken history and no current shell-backed+auto caller in this repo (checked: no production caller constructs both together). Not fixed here since it is a distinct code path from what this phase actually drove and verified end to end, and changing gate auto-resolution capacity semantics is a production behavior change outside "add lifecycle acceptance". Flagging so a future pass can decide whether auto-resolved shell-backed gates need the same capacity binding, or whether the combination is intentionally unsupported/never occurs.

Delivered real (not hand-authored) monitor and gate-shell weighted-capacity lifecycle acceptance in tests/fakey/: extracted the shared _RunnerSlotFakeyHarness into a new tests/fakey/_runner_slot_harness.py (toobig limit forced the split), and added tests/fakey/test_monitor_gate_capacity_e2e.py with 6 tests, replacing the prior hand-authored monitor simulation.

1) test_weight_two_land_family_retains_one_owner_through_real_monitor_and_next_handoff: drives real sase.monitor.start.start_monitor (real detached supervisor subprocess) and real sase.monitor.followup.launch_followup_agent (only spawn_agent_subprocess mocked, to substitute a real fakey successor) through a weight-2 land family. Asserts the persisted runner_claim_owner_key/queue_weight/queue_weight_explicit are identical across starter, monitor, and successor, and that weight-2 competitors park against the family before/during/after, with a fresh competitor introduced only once each holder is confirmed live (a finished monitor with no successor yet legitimately holds zero, so racing a live competitor through that real handoff gap is flaky by construction, not a bug).
2) test_independently_weighted_parallel_member_and_its_serial_successor_keep_own_lineage: a parallel member (agent_family_parallel=True) sharing a live land family's display name gets its own distinct owner key; its serial successor (admitted while the parallel predecessor is still live, matching the verified serial-overlap dedup contract) reuses that owner key, never the land family's, proven via a real weight-sized competitor.
3) Gate routes, via bind_gate_shell_execution_callbacks + execute_gate_selection real wait_for_runner_slot contention: pending gate shell holds zero capacity (unrelated agents admit around it unaffected by its declared weight); the synchronous/default answer route claims and releases capacity like an ordinary agent without disturbing an unrelated owner's claim; the --detach route (real CLI dispatch, submit_proc_request mocked only to avoid a real background process, then the identical captured re-invocation argv driven for real on a thread) reaches the same real claim path with real contention.
4) test_gate_cancellation_and_failed_startup_do_not_disturb_an_unrelated_owners_claim: cancelling a still-pending gate, and a gate command whose executable bit is stripped after valid creation (real command_start_failed), both leave a concurrently-live unrelated owner's runner_claim_owner_key untouched.
